summary: This motion will give the City Solicitor authority to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's decision approving the applications for consent and minor variance respecting 65 Fortieth Street (Application Nos.: B0016/18EYK, A0127/18EYK, and A0137/18EYK) (collectively, the "Applications") to the Toronto Local Appeal Body (the "LPAT"). In order to meet the appeal deadline of February 13, 2019 and crystalize the City's appeal rights for these applications, the City Solicitor has already appealed this matter to the TLAB. As a result, this matter is time sensitive and urgent and is required to allow the City to continue with this appeal. On January 24, 2019, the Etobicoke District Panel of the Committee of Adjustment (the "Committee") approved an application related to the property municipally known as 65 Fortieth Street for consent to sever and two associated applications for minor variances (collectively the "Applications"). The Applications seek to demolish the existing residential dwelling, sever the subject property into two residential lots, and build two new single detached dwellings with integral garages. The Applications required various variances to City-wide Zoning By-law No. 569-2013 such as for lot frontage, lot area, and floor space index. In a report from the Supervisor, Tree Protection and Plan Review – West District, dated May 10, 2018, Urban Forestry Staff is opposed…
decided: City Council on February 26, 2019, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's decisions regarding consent and minor variance Applications B0016/18EYK, A0127/18EYK, and A0137/18EYK respecting 65 Fortieth Street. 2. City Council authorize the City Solicitor and appropriate City staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing to oppose Applications B0016/18EYK, A0127/18EYK and A0137/18EYK respecting 65 Fortieth Street, and to retain outside consultants as necessary. 3. City Council authorize the City Solicitor to resolve the appeals at the City Solicitor's discretion and in consultation with the Ward Councillor and the Director of Community Planning, Etobicoke York District.
